usage.notes: Start with versioned build-time snapshots for stable anatomical IDs, spatial reference objects and semantic relationships. Runtime API access can be enabled later behind a Panacea adapter with caching, timeout and graceful fallback rather than coupling UI components directly to HRA services.

license.scope: The HuBMAP HRA-KG repository states that its code is MIT licensed and its data is CC BY 4.0. This registry entry covers that HRA-KG scope. Any third-party upstream source or separately hosted 3D asset must retain its own provenance/license record and must not inherit this permission automatically.
license.notes: Preserve HRA attribution and version identity. Treat separately sourced reference objects as separate assets when their own entry/license metadata exists.

validation.notes: Use HRA to organize reference anatomy, spatial relationships, anatomical structures, cell types and biomarkers. It is a reference atlas, not a patient-specific diagnostic model and not sufficient by itself for clinical decisions.

provenance.notes: Persist HRA release/version, digital object identifier, source ontology/atlas identifiers and transformation history. Preserve semantic IDs across mesh optimization so visual geometry remains linked to the reference graph.

adapter.notes: Planned pipeline: HRA digital object/graph -> version and license gate -> normalize stable anatomical/cell/biomarker IDs -> map optional reference geometry -> Panacea Human Graph -> Body Explorer selection and zoom hierarchy.
